Universal Purchase settings vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's Universal Purchase workflow covers language. Connect and iOS actually separate purchase linking from storefront copy:

  • Universal Purchase linking — associates one paid app record across iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Vision so a single purchase unlocks supported platforms. Does not generate Chinese text.
  • Platform binaries and entitlements — iOS, macOS, and visionOS builds submitted separately. Packaging and signing are engineering — not listing copy.
  • Cross-platform product page — one shared listing on the China storefront with platform availability badges Apple renders from your Connect configuration. Badge chrome may localize; your name, subtitle, description, and screenshot overlays do not unless you fill zh-Hans fields.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Universal Purchase flags.

A compliant US listing with Universal Purchase enabled and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Universal Purchase listing copy vs per-device screenshot sets vs platform-only pages

US/EU indie teams often conflate three string families on multi-platform apps. This page covers product-page listing copy that markets one purchase across devices — not per-device gallery matrices or platform-only listings:

  • Universal Purchase marketing on the shared product page — description paragraphs, subtitle cross-platform positioning, and screenshot overlays like "Buy once, use on all your devices", "Universal Purchase", and "Available on iPhone, iPad, and Mac". This page.
  • Per-device screenshot sets — separate iPad, Mac, and Watch upload matrices on the same zh-Hans row when buyers browse on that hardware. Covered on our iPad, Mac & Watch screenshots guide — not the cross-platform purchase story on default listing fields.
  • visionOS-only or tvOS-only product pages — separate platform tabs with their own name, subtitle, and spatial or TV screenshot sets. See visionOS listing guide or tvOS listing guide — not Universal Purchase badge copy on the main shared page.

You can localize the title and still leave every Universal Purchase screenshot overlay and description paragraph English-only. What China buyers see when zh-Hans Universal Purchase copy is missing

Cross-platform purchasers browsing the China App Store evaluate one-purchase value in the first scroll. Common failure modes when only en-US is filled:

  • English title and subtitle — app name and tagline still Latin script while competitors show native Chinese cross-platform positioning
  • Untranslated Universal Purchase badges on screenshots — overlay lines like "Buy once, use on all your devices", "Universal Purchase", "One app, all your Apple devices", or "Available on iPhone, iPad, and Mac" remain English on zh-Hans gallery frames
  • Cross-platform value in English — description opens with US multi-device marketing ("Works everywhere you do") that China readers skim past or misread
  • Keyword field still en-US — buyers search 通用购买, 一次购买, 全平台, or 多设备; an English-only keyword row misses China Search intent
  • Mixed page — Chinese description pasted once but screenshot captions and subtitle still English — reads unfinished next to localized competitors
  • Formal machine translation — stiff 翻译腔 for "Universal Purchase" (通用购买 vs 一次购买多设备) and wrong platform lists that omit Apple Vision or Mac when your app actually ships there

Better zh-Hans listing copy helps cross-platform buyers understand one-purchase value before install. It does not replace Universal Purchase configuration, binary submission, or Apple's review decisions.

Universal Purchase–specific listing copy — what translates differently

Cross-platform listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe buying once across Apple devices — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Buy once, all devices phrasing

US pages use "Buy once, use on all your devices", "Universal Purchase", or "One purchase, every platform." China storefront copy often uses 一次购买，全设备可用, 通用购买, or 多平台通用 — depending on whether you mean Apple's Universal Purchase feature or a generic cross-platform promise. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual Connect Universal Purchase setup, not inventing platform support your app does not ship.

Platform list accuracy

Screenshot overlays and description leads name supported hardware — iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Vision. Chinese buyers expect an accurate platform list (iPhone、iPad、Mac、Apple Vision) rather than English slogans ("Works on all your Apple devices") that hide which platforms you actually support.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need cross-platform search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 通用版, 全平台, and 多设备 each signal different intent from generic productivity keywords.

Caption lines vs burned-in badges

Apple may render Universal Purchase availability from Connect configuration, but marketing screenshot overlays you control — "Buy once, use on all your devices" headlines on gallery frames — are separate caption fields or burned-in PNG text. See Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese for caption-field mechanics when overlays are editable in Connect.

Common mistakes on Universal Purchase zh-Hans listings

  • Assuming Universal Purchase linking localizes automatically — platform SKUs linked; zh-Hans row never added or left blank
  • Only translating the description — subtitle, keywords, and screenshot caption lines still English
  • Reusing US Universal Purchase badges verbatim — Latin badges on zh-Hans screenshots signal an unfinished localization
  • Conflating listing copy with Connect configuration — description explains how to enable Universal Purchase in Settings instead of what the buyer gets; setup instructions belong in support docs, not AppLocale scope
  • Mixing up this page with per-device screenshot work — iPad/Mac gallery captions localized but cross-platform purchase story still English on subtitle and description; or the reverse
  • Ignoring caption fields per localization — zh-Hans screenshot set uploaded but overlay text fields never saved; see Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese
  • Expecting AppLocale to enable Universal Purchase — Connect linking, binary submission, and entitlement work are outside listing rewrite

Connect checklist before you order Universal Purchase listing copy

  1. Confirm China under Pricing and Availability — storefront enabled if you intend to sell there
